title: Database inventory, structural domain and coverage boundary

units.raw_row: one row of bde_db_full.csv.gz (one bond instance in one molecule)
units.unique_fragment_pair: distinct (molecule, fragment1, fragment2); bond_type and bde are constant inside a unit
units.benchmark_observation: one of the 543 experimental rows (error-analysis unit)

3_structural_domain.hac_definition: heavy-atom count of parent SMILES, RDKit GetNumHeavyAtoms

5_exhaustiveness_supplement.note: completeness = db unique fragment pairs / symmetry-unique bonds (capped at 1.0)

2_inflation_note: A (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) unit is stored once per equivalent bond instance: symmetry-equivalent atoms (e.g. the four H of methane) yield several rows with identical fragments and identical bde. C-H has 2.145 rows per pair because methyl/methylene H atoms are numerous and symmetry-equivalent; O-O/H-O/N-N have essentially one row per pair.

4_out_of_db_decomposition.interpretation: The benchmark extends past the database in molecular size: 150/543 observations (27.6%) have a parent with HAC 11-38 while the database stops at HAC 10. Element coverage does NOT explain any gap: every benchmark parent contains only C/N/O, which is exactly the database element set. A further 24 observations have HAC <= 10 but their parent is simply not in the database.
